correctness.finding: PASS. For a test family Z, the Euclidean weak-residual norm is exactly ||T_Zw||_2^2=<S_Zw,w>, while T_Z^*G^dagger T_Z is the orthogonal projector onto span(Z); hence Gram-inverse weighting is basis-invariant and Euclidean weighting agrees with the physical energy metric on the span exactly for a tight frame. In the submitted two-dimensional example, b=(1,(1+eps^2)^(-1/2)) and J=(0,eps(1+eps^2)^(-1/2))^T give the exact Gauss--Newton correction xi=1/eps. The source sign convention then produces energy error sqrt(1+eps^{-2}) while the measured Euclidean residual decreases. Solving kappa=(1+c)/(1-c), c=(1+eps^2)^(-1/2), gives exactly |xi|=(sqrt(kappa)-1/sqrt(kappa))/2 and amplification=(sqrt(kappa)+1/sqrt(kappa))/2. I independently recomputed these identities at eps=1,0.1,0.01.

originality.finding: PASS, narrowly scoped. Rojas et al. already establish that classical VPINN weak-residual losses depend on the chosen basis and advocate the inverse-Gram discrete dual norm; frame operators and tight-frame characterizations are standard. Those mechanisms are not new. The motivating 2026 Gauss--Newton/Petrov--Galerkin paper uses finite weak measurements and ordinary Euclidean least squares in its general construction. Targeted searches did not locate the submitted source-specific result that individually energy-normalized tests with a fixed test span can force an arbitrarily destructive one-step Gauss--Newton correction, nor the exact square-root frame-condition-number amplification law.

scientific_value.finding: PASS. The counterexample isolates a concrete failure mode that individual test normalization does not control: near-linear dependence can make the algorithm's own least-squares objective improve while the physical energy error diverges. This is a useful diagnostic for the newly proposed weak Gauss--Newton framework. The record appropriately does not claim failure of the reported benchmarks or novelty for the Gram-inverse remedy.

Damping, regularization, trust regions, adaptive tests or well-conditioned/tight test families can prevent the pathology.
